resources.string: This car\'s OBD doesn\'t report fuel. Learn it from the CANbox instead: needs root.
No fuel level yet. Connect the OBD adapter: not every car reports it.

Set the level your dash gauge shows, tap Capture A, then close this and use the car normally. Days later, once the gauge has dropped a little, reopen, set the new value and tap Capture B. Capture A is saved across restarts. Only bytes that moved with the fuel are offered.
Set the fuel level your dash shows, then tap Capture A.
Captured A at %1$d%% (saved). You can close this and drive normally, come back once the gauge drops a few %%, set the new value, then Capture B.
A and B are at the same level. Capture B at a different fuel level.
No byte tracked the change. Recapture B after a bigger drop.
Bytes that moved with the fuel
Open the head unit\'s trip computer and type the range (km to empty) it shows, then tap Search. Pick the signal whose live value keeps matching the trip computer.
No signal holds that value. Check the number, leave the trip computer open a few seconds and search again.
Signals holding that value: pick the one that follows the trip computer
No paired Bluetooth devices. Pair your OBD adapter in Bluetooth settings first.
The engine computer didn\'t answer the fault-code request. Try again in a moment.
The engine lamp is on but no code came through. Try again with the engine running.
Engine off: with the ignition on, the engine lamp lights up as a self-test and goes out once the engine runs. The scan repeats by itself once the engine is running.
Standard OBD only sees engine and emissions faults; ABS, airbag and body warnings need Citroën\'s diagnostic tool.
Adapter replied \"%1$s\". Turn ignition ON (engine off) and retry.
Doors CLOSED → Capture A. Then OPEN the door → Capture B. Only discrete signals that differ are shown.
Capture A (closed), then B (open) to compare.
No clean discrete difference. Do it with the engine OFF so sensors don\'t drift, and keep the door open during Capture B.
Check spark plugs & coils (THP: coils are a known weak point), fuel injectors, and for vacuum leaks. Do plugs/coils as a set.
Swap coil/plug from cyl 1 to another cyl; if the misfire follows, replace that coil/plug. Also check injector 1.
Swap coil/plug to isolate; check injector 2 and compression.
Swap coil/plug to isolate; check injector 3 and compression.
Swap coil/plug to isolate; check injector 4 and compression.
Classic 1.6 THP stretched timing chain. Check chain, tensioner and cam/crank sensors. Often needs a timing chain kit.
Likely stretched timing chain / tensioner (1.6 THP). Inspect chain & sprockets.
VVT/cam phaser or oil control valve. Check oil level/quality, VVT solenoid, and timing chain wear.
Check the cam sensor and its wiring; verify timing (chain) is correct.
Test/replace cam sensor; inspect connector and wiring.
Common on THP/HDi. Check for boost leaks (hoses/intercooler), wastegate/turbo actuator, and the diverter valve.
Check wastegate actuator sticking, boost solenoid, and for a stuck VNT (HDi).
HDi: check fuel filter, low-pressure supply, high-pressure pump and rail pressure regulator; look for air/leaks.
Check the rail pressure regulator/metering valve and pump; inspect fuel filter.
HDi: inspect injector leak-off, high-pressure pipes and pump seals for diesel leaks.
Often a worn catalytic converter or a lazy rear O2 sensor. Rule out exhaust leaks and misfires first.
Clean or replace the EGR valve; check EGR cooler and passages for carbon (common on HDi).
Check EGR valve stuck open and its control; clean carbon build-up.
HDi diesel: do a long highway run for regeneration; check DPF pressure sensor and additive (Eolys) level. May need forced regen.
DPF near end of life or blocked; may need forced regen or DPF cleaning/replacement.
Check IAT sensor and wiring/connector; clean or replace the sensor (often in the MAF/intake).
Usually a stuck-open thermostat. Replace thermostat; verify coolant level and sensor.
Check the upstream O2 sensor heater circuit and fuse; replace the sensor if the heater is open.
Inspect upstream O2 sensor and wiring; replace if lazy/faulty.
Check for intake/vacuum leaks (common), dirty MAF, weak fuel pump/injectors.
Check for leaking injectors, high fuel pressure, dirty MAF or faulty O2 sensor.
Clean throttle body; check for intake leaks and throttle motor operation.
Check throttle body motor and wiring; may need throttle body replacement.
No stored description. Scan for related codes, check the affected circuit\'s sensor/wiring, and search \"%1$s Citroën C4 Picasso\" for model-specific guidance.
Pairing: enter the adapter\'s PIN in the dialog (often 1234 or 0000)
Switching on the head unit\'s Bluetooth…
Bluetooth is off on the head unit
%1$s is not paired with the head unit: tap OBD to pair it again
Pairing with %1$s did not finish: tap OBD and enter its PIN (often 1234 or 0000)
The head unit\'s Bluetooth is off and won\'t switch on: restart the head unit, then tap OBD
Android\'s Bluetooth on the head unit is stuck: restart the head unit, then tap OBD
%1$s refused the connection: taken by a phone or another app, unpowered, or out of range
%1$s connected but never answered: switch the ignition on, then tap OBD
OBD goes through the phone: link the phone first
OBD goes through the phone: choose the adapter in the companion
Asking the phone for the adapter
The phone could not reach %1$s: check it is plugged in and paired with the phone
OBD is paused during the call and comes back when it ends
Android Auto on %1$s is blocking the OBD adapter
The phone and the OBD adapter share the head unit\'s Bluetooth. Android Auto on the phone keeps trying to start without a cable and takes it over.
On the phone, open Settings, then Apps, then Android Auto.
Tap Permissions, then Nearby devices, and choose Don\'t allow.
Turn the car off and on again.
Calls, music and Android Auto with a USB cable keep working.
Android Auto on %1$s is blocking OBD. The steps to fix it are on the screen.
Connect with the OBD button in the bar
Added to the speed the car reports, to match its speedometer
Speed now: %1$d km/h. Adjust until it matches your speedometer.
Connect the OBD adapter to see the corrected speed live.
They are erased from the car for good. A garage needs them to find a fault.
